newsitem.title: INDIA: India does not plan to raise oil prices - minister.
newsitem.headline: India does not plan to raise oil prices - minister.

text.p: Indian Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu said on Friday that the government had no plan to raise the domestic prices of petroleum products despite a burgeoning subsidy bill.
"Actually there is no hike of prices. We are not intending to hike the price of petroleum products," Balu told Asian News International (ANI), a local news agency.
The minister said the government would owe state-controlled oil firms 158 billion rupees ($4.4 billion) by the end of March, up from 57 billion rupees one year earlier.
The oil companies have been pressing Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government to increase prices as a means of raising the funds needed to repay the money.
The shortfall, called the oil pool deficit, is the amount the government owes oil companies for selling petroleum products to Indian consumers way below world prices.
Oil companies shoulder the burden of the deficit while they wait for the state to pay them back, but the increasing strain on their liquidity is forcing companies to borrow.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Balu as telling reporters that "the deficit will have to be managed by some other means".

Balu told ANI: "Let us see what happens in the budget." He was referring to the government's budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting on April 1, scheduled to be presented to parliament later on Friday.
Balu said he expected duties on petroleum products to be adjusted in the budget.
"Let us see what happens, what is fixed, what relaxed duty structure is there in the budget. I expect some duty structure rationalisation," Balu told ANI.
Oil analysts in Bombay recently said the government was expected to cut import tariffs for crude oil and might raise them for refined products in the 1997/98 budget.
If the differentials between crude and product tariffs were restructured, it would be a key step towards liberalising the refining industry, analysts said. ($1 = 35.9 rupees)
